notes.title: Developement progress
notes.notes: [p][b]Hello everyone![/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]Let’s share a few words about where we stand with the development of the promised ScribeRPG demo.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]As you might expect, we're mostly fixing bugs and polishing content. No surprise there - it probably sounds like the classic game dev line when trying to look super busy. 😉 But trust us, in our case, it's absolutely true.[/p][p]Our bug list grew, especially after we completely rewrote how the game handles controls. We did this not only to support fully customizable controls, but also to ensure that [i]any[/i] type of controller works with Scribe RPG. It might sound routine, but this change was a major challenge for us.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45058922/28e2c50be6ecfab8abc37847bd65de166e030d80.jpg"][/img][/p][p]But we did it, and now the game easily recognizes controllers and switches to the correct bindings automatically.[/p][p]That gave us a solid foundation for the next big step: [b]Steam Deck support.[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45058922/83636ed77a20a5d01e678e6cfee91d557fe60e29.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We believe our game is perfect for Steam Deck users, so we want to make sure the experience is as smooth as possible. There’s still some polishing to do, but it’s already running—and we’re super excited about it! 😊[/p][p] [/p][previewyoutube="SD0x3u8YLaY;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][b]We truly appreciate our steadily growing community across all socials and are incredibly grateful for every Wishlist addition your support and sharing bring us.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Wishing everyone a great summer![/p][p]Rawmeat dev team[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: NPC patrol an navigation
notes.notes:
[b]Hello everyone!

We've just successfully implemented our advanced patrol and navigation system for NPCs![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45058922/20ffae18a998f06a5778cfead2f7277bf2cbb0ec.gif[/img]

As simple as this feature might seem, it took us much longer than expected - but we’re certain it was worth the effort.

Originally, we planned for classic NPC behavior, like in most action platformers. This meant NPCs would mindlessly walk back and forth, waiting for the player to show up and then get clobbered. Since our game has many other features, we thought simple NPC behavior like this would be enough.

[b]But we changed our minds.[/b] 🙂

[previewyoutube=8cmZalnpCv0;full][/previewyoutube]

We decided to let NPCs move through the world just like the player can, actively chasing player and navigating the obstacles of our organic environment. This has added a whole new level of dynamic gameplay, creating unpredictable encounters throughout Scribe RPG.

Now, we’re charging full steam ahead toward finishing our free demo, fixing bugs, and polishing everything up.

Wish us strength - and if you’d like to support us, please share or wishlist our game. We’d greatly appreciate it!

[b]Team Rawmeat[/b]

notes.title: Scribe RPG Development Update
notes.notes:
After a long period of radio silence - when we were fully focused on development - we’re excited to say we’re back up to full speed! Our goal is to release a playable demo of the game soon for all of you to check out and, hopefully, enjoy.

[list]
[*] [b]What we have:[/b]
[/list]
The entire demo and all its content are already in place! We’re now fine-tuning the writing, quests, and other gameplay elements, as well as finalizing the graphics and sound.

[list]
[*] [b]What we are working on:[/b]
[/list]
We’re wrapping up and fine-tuning our combat mechanics, and most importantly, we’re implementing a robust navigation system for our NPCs. Originally, this wasn’t something we had planned for the game. However, NPCs patrolling the world or actively chasing the player - using everything the player can, like ropes, ladders, platforms, and ledges - felt like a must-have. We believe it greatly enhances gameplay versatility.

Please stay tuned much more will come soon :)

[previewyoutube=fHopxqbCOg4;full][/previewyoutube]
